commentary_title: Atlantic Basin congestion continues to absorb prompt VLCC tonnage and support freight rates.
commentary_summary: The VLCC market remained firm, as utilisation stood at 90.8% despite slowdown in tonne-mile demand. With the tonne-mile index falling to 82.2, the persistence of strong vessel employment highlights the role of congestion, vessel positioning inefficiencies and tighter effective supply in underpinning freight market performance. | Effective VLCC supply remained constrained by persistent congestion particularly across the Atlantic Basin. A sharp increase in western anchorage volumes, combined with higher global tonnage waiting at anchor, continued to absorb available capacity and support spot freight markets. | Asia continued to underpin global VLCC activity, with China, India and the broader Pacific Basin accounting for the largest concentration of both laden and ballast tonnage. While congestion at key discharge hubs has eased from the elevated levels seen earlier in the year, anchorage volumes remain above historical averages, reflecting sustained crude import demand across the region.
